items.title: Marshall Lawrence Interview, 1960-06-28
items.q: Roby Sho used to play, I remember too. ... We used to play that

ctx.x: Meet me by the Watermill and Vine, my lending loop?

Uh-huh, and meet the old cherry on the... Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Well, I can remember a piece that we used to play, it was not right after... When I first began to play, Here Come Your Daddy Now. Roby Sho used to play, I remember too. Here Come Your Daddy Now, Oh Pop, Oh Pop, Oh Pop. Or So Mom, or something like that. Uh-huh. We used to play that, uh... Not when I first began, though. It was maybe a little while ago. I'll tell you what, if I can think of some of this. Every once in a while, uh... When I think of a piece…

Well, why don't you write those down and then drop me a postcard next time you're coming to New Orleans, and I'll wait by the telephone at work, you know? I can... Yeah. Just write me that you've come and what time, and when you'll phone me at my work number. Yeah. I'll be up there working, you know?
